svg.title: How bacterial meningitis develops (single colour)
svg.desc: Bacteria spread in droplets and are carried in the nose and throat; some invade the bloodstream, cross into the meninges, and draw neutrophils into the cerebrospinal fluid, which a lumbar puncture samples. The usual causes differ with age: group B streptococcus, Escherichia coli and Listeria in newborns; meningococcus, pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b in older babies and children.
